title: Reclaim Initiative - Token Budget Orchestration & Latency‑Safe Quant Profiles
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Unit token costs and tail latency are the two biggest levers we can pull to reduce hosted spend without harming product UX. Reclaim is a focused initiative to orchestrate per-customer token budgets, apply latency-safe quantization profiles, and expose low-friction controls in Console so product teams can set cost/quality tradeoffs by cohort.

Goals: 1) Reduce median per-customer token spend by 12% on pilot cohort within 8 weeks. 2) Ensure P95 latency degradation <= 5% for enabled quant profiles. 3) Ship Console controls + rollout policy for token budgets and auto-fallback. 4) Instrument reliable success metrics and alerts for quality regressions.

Scope: - Server-side enforcement of per-key token budgets and soft throttles. - Adaptive model selection: prefer smaller/quantized variants when budget thresholds hit, with latency guardrails. - Latency-safe quant profiles: pre-validated quantization settings per model class plus a canary process. - Console UX + API for setting budgets, viewing savings, and scheduling rollouts. - Eval harness and prompt-level signal capture for regressions.

Non-goals: - Broad wholesale re-quantization of all models in catalog (we'll only propose profiles and run focused pilots). - Re-implement cost billing pipelines (we read usage metrics from existing pipeline).

Success metrics: - Cohort token spend delta (percentage). - P95 latency change pre/post. - Quality regression rate (eval score drop > delta threshold) per model/version. - Number of customer-reported incidents tied to Reclaim controls.

Milestones: - Week 0-2: Define safe quant profiles and run offline evals. - Week 3-4: Implement per-key budget enforcement and soft-throttle API. - Week 5: Console control UI + rollout policy authoring. - Week 6-7: Canary pilot with 3 internal customers; realtime monitoring dashboards. - Week 8: Expand to 10 customers or rollback based on metrics.

Rollout and rollback: Default is a staged rollout with automated guard rails: if quality regression OR P95 latency > 5% relative increase OR customer support tickets rise above threshold, we automatically opt affected keys back to full fidelity model and surface an incident in Console.

Risks and mitigations: - Risk: Silent quality regressions. Mitigation: store prompt snippets and run lightweight eval checks post-change; require manual approval for profiles that exceed per-prompt delta. - Risk: Budget enforcement causes user-visible truncation. Mitigation: soft-throttle mode first (latency-preserving windowing) and customer-visible warning headers. - Risk: Cross-service dependencies (billing/quotas). Mitigation: early alignment with billing and platform infra owners (ENG-22114).

Open questions: - What threshold of eval delta is acceptable per product vertical? (Owner: PM + Product leads) - Should budgets be token-based only or include per-request cost units? (Owner:ENG + PM) - How to surface rollback rationale clearly in Console for non-engineering customers?

Artifacts and links: - Design mockups: drive.redwood/internals/reclaim-ui (link placeholder) - Eval harness PR: github.com/redwood/reclaim-evals/pull/12 - Infra spike notes: confluence.redwood/s/reclaim-infra-spike

2026-02-18 — Marco Ruiz: Completed enforcement API prototype. Soft-throttle behaviour validated in staging with synthetic workload. Next: wire usage metrics for per-key counters (dependency: ENG-30201).
2026-02-25 — Lina Gomez: Initial Console mockups uploaded. UX decision: expose 'budget schedule' (daily/weekly) plus an emergency override. Need acceptance criteria for visibility of rollback events.

2026-03-03 — Rui Chen: Offline evals for three quant profiles across 5 representative prompts show mean BLEU-like delta < 0.8% and 95th latency improvement of ~18% on A100-qa instances. Marking profiles as candidate-safe, but need more diverse prompt types before canary.

2026-03-08 — Marco Ruiz: Canary started for internal cohort alpha-1 (traffic shredded into 10% of users). Early telemetry shows token spend down 9% without quality alarms. P95 latency stable. Expanding to partner trial next week.

2026-03-10 — Aisha Patel: PM sync notes: shortlist for next steps — (1) add rollback reason taxonomy in Console, (2) tighten eval gating for longer prompts, (3) define SLA for partner trial and sign consent doc. Assigned owner tasks and updated milestone dates.
